subject.title: refactor(cron): split oversized modules, retire max-lines suppressions, behavior-name regression suites

question: Should this protected cron refactor merge once the remaining checks complete and a real isolated-cron delivery run confirms the extracted execution and delivery seams preserve behavior?
rationale: The patch is intentionally large and behavior-neutral, but it relocates runtime execution and message-delivery logic; the protected maintainer label requires an explicit owner judgment on whether focused test evidence plus live proof is sufficient.

options.title: Require focused live proof
options.body: Request a redacted run showing an isolated cron job is created, executes, and reaches its configured delivery target after the final checks pass.

options.title: Accept test-only evidence
options.body: Merge after the remaining exact-head checks pass if the cron owners judge the existing focused suites and contract checks sufficient for this internal refactor.

options.title: Split follow-up work
options.body: Land only the mechanical test-renaming and max-lines changes now, and move execution/delivery extraction into smaller follow-up PRs.

recommendation.title: Require focused live proof
recommendation.body: Request a redacted run showing an isolated cron job is created, executes, and reaches its configured delivery target after the final checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the extraction boundaries and the follow-up visibility restriction, so they are the clearest available routing candidate for explaining or demonstrating the intended preserved behavior.
